Title: MetaTrans: human drug metabolites
Description: Drugs are reshaped in the liver by phase I and phase II reactions that can blunt efficacy or create toxic metabolites, so the likely products matter early. MetaTrans casts biotransformation as translation, fine-tuning a molecular transformer pre-trained on general chemical reactions with curated human metabolic reactions and combining six fine-tuned models whose predictions are pooled. Decoding uses beam search rather than sampling, so the same input always returns the same metabolites in the same order (up to thirty, best-ranked first), with no indication of the enzyme, the rate or whether the metabolite accumulates.
Interpretation: Up to thirty human metabolites generated deterministically by beam search from the input compound, ordered by how early the six models propose them (columns metabolite_00 onwards; most inputs give fewer than thirty).
